title: SharePoint: SharePoint agents in Teams mobile group chats and meetings
summary: The roadmap facts, control paths, commands and permissions statements are supported. The briefing appropriately leaves the mobile rollout and default unconfirmed; its general pay-as-you-go statements should be narrowed to existing .agent files because upgraded agents follow a different licensing model.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap description mentions using agents but no new actions, autonomous behaviour or new data access.
claims.quote: Use SharePoint agents in Teams Mobile group chats and meetings.

claims.claim: Agents in SharePoint access organisational data the same way Copilot in other Microsoft 365 apps does.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint access your organization's data the same way Copilot in other Microsoft 365 apps does, responding to users based on their access permissions to the data.

claims.claim: Agents in SharePoint use SharePoint sites, pages and document libraries as knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint use SharePoint sites, pages, and document libraries as knowledge sources to respond to the user.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An agent's responses depend on each user's permissions to its data sources.
claims.quote: For users who access and use an agent in SharePoint, the agent's responses depend on each user's permissions to the agent's data sources.

claims.claim: Permissions on a .agent file determine who can access or edit that agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: An existing SharePoint agent shared in Teams responds based on the permissions of the person asking the question.
claims.quote: The agent responds based on the permissions of the person asking the question. When you share an agent with others, they can only access the sources for which they have permissions.

claims.claim: Sharing the agent in Teams does not automatically change permissions on its sources.
claims.quote: The permissions for the sites, pages, and files included in the agent don't automatically adjust when the agent is shared.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents generally do not require activation.
claims.quote: Agents in SharePoint don't require activation.

claims.quote: Currently, users with a Microsoft Copilot license can use the agents.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[2].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Users without a Microsoft Copilot licence can be covered by SharePoint agents pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: For users who aren't assigned with a Microsoft Copilot license, you can control user access to agents through pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.fix: Narrow the repeated general pay-as-you-go wording in licensing.notes, Cost and licensing, controls[2].note and the cost rationale to: 'For existing .agent files, users without a Microsoft Copilot licence can be covered by SharePoint agents pay-as-you-go billing.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/upgrade-sharepoint-agents, which states: 'SharePoint Agents pay-as-you-go only applies to .agent files. The upgraded agents follow the capabilities and licensing model for agents in Microsoft Copilot app.'

claims.claim: For the pay-as-you-go access route, only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access.
claims.quote: Only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access to agents.

claims.claim: Tenant admins can manage actively used SharePoint agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage actively used agents in SharePoint in the Microsoft 365 admin center, under the Agents section of the Copilot Control System

claims.claim: AI admins can manage actively used SharePoint agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage actively used agents in SharePoint in the Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.claim: Existing .agent files continue working across SharePoint, Teams and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.
claims.quote: Existing agents in the .agent file format will continue to work across SharePoint, Microsoft Teams, and the Copilot app until the end of March 2027.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: .agent files stop responding after March 2027.
claims.quote: After March 2027, .agent files will stop responding and you will have to upgrade to continue using them.

claims.claim: Existing .agent agents can currently be used in a Teams chat or channel.
claims.quote: You might currently use these agents in the SharePoint chat pane, through the Agent Link web part, in the agent immersive viewer, in a Microsoft Teams chat or channel, or in the Copilot app.

claims.claim: After March 2027, users of .agent files added to Teams chats see an upgrade-required message.
claims.quote: .agent files that you added to a Teams chat or channel stop responding. Users will see a message indicating it needs to be upgraded before it can be used.

claims.claim: The block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: The package block operation is a beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking an agent created using SharePoint only affects its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The documented block for existing SharePoint agents does not yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint or Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. Select the site you want to configure. Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site ... Use PowerShell ... Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery removes AI entry points on a SharePoint site, including creating agents.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery also removes AI-powered entry points from these SharePoint sites. Users don't see entry points such as the Copilot button, AI actions menus (including creating agents), or Create pages with AI.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits discovery of selected sites' content in organisation-wide search and Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery leaves permissions unchanged and users retain direct access to content they can already access.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires the organisation to have a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery requires SharePoint Advanced Management availability and links its prerequisites.
claims.quote: You can configure Restricted Content Discovery if your organization is licensed for Copilot and has SharePoint Advanced Management available. See Prerequisites for SharePoint Advanced Management.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.claim: Licences are assigned at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least a License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: The existing SharePoint agent experience has a mixed licensing model of Microsoft Copilot entitlement and pay-as-you-go use.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Existing .agent pay-as-you-go usage is metered under Copilot Studio on the Azure invoice, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice. ... Your organization receives an invoice for all Azure services used at the end of each month.
